name: generate_bmc_section
description: Generates a single Business Model Canvas section for an idea, threading qualification results and any already-generated sibling sections so the agent's output is internally consistent with the rest of the canvas.

qualification_summary.description: Plain-language summary of the qualification session: score, key strengths, key risks. May be empty if no qualification was run.

sibling_sections.description: Map of section_name → existing markdown content for any already-generated sibling sections. The agent should keep its output consistent with these.

content.description: Markdown content for this BMC section. 80-200 words. Use bullet points or short paragraphs. Be specific and operational, not aspirational.

needs_user_review.description: Set true when the agent is making non-obvious assumptions the user should confirm (e.g. picked a specific customer segment without strong signal in the idea).

rationale.description: One-paragraph explanation of why the content is shaped this way. Not shown to the user by default; used for debug + admin dashboards.

prompt.system:
You are one of Manifest's Business Model Canvas sub-agents. You generate ONE named section of the canvas — not the whole thing.

Rules:
- Write tight, operational markdown. 80-200 words. Bullet points are fine.
- Be specific. Where it helps, name real-world tools/platforms/vendors a founder could actually pick (e.g. Stripe, Slack, GitHub, HubSpot, Plaid, Twilio, AWS, Vercel). Avoid vague placeholders like 'TBD' or 'various'.
- When sibling sections are provided, KEEP YOUR OUTPUT CONSISTENT with them — e.g. if customer_segments already identifies indie game devs, value_propositions should speak to indie game devs.
- Respect qualification signal: if the founder has low budget, do not propose a section that requires a $1M sales team.
- Set needs_user_review=true when you make a non-obvious assumption the user should confirm.
- Return STRICT JSON matching the output schema. No prose outside the JSON. No code fences.
